meta.label: Cat food
meta.attribution: Health and transparency scores are built only from FDA recall and safety-alert pages, company recall notices filed with FDA, CDC outbreak reporting, and independent food-safety journalism about a specific inspection or incident; where a search of FDA's own recall and safety-alert listings on the date shown found nothing for a brand, the note says exactly that, and that is an absence of a public record rather than a claim the brand is risk free. Price and availability come only from a company's own site or a retailer's own page describing its distribution, so most cells here are sparse: a fact that could not be verified from an acceptable source was left out rather than guessed. Transparency describes what a company's own materials or FDA inspection findings show about its manufacturing and sourcing. Reviewed 2026. Suggest corrections through Contribute.

products.name: Purina Cat Chow
products.description: Nestlé Purina's original dry cat food line, sold widely in US grocery and mass retail stores.

health.note: On December 26, 2025, third-party distributor Gold Star Distribution recalled all FDA-regulated products held at its Minneapolis warehouse, including Purina Cat Chow Complete dry cat food, after an FDA inspection found rodent droppings, rodent urine, and bird droppings in storage areas. The contamination was at the distributor's warehouse, not at a Purina manufacturing plant, and the notice said no illnesses had been reported to date.

transparency.note: Independent food-safety journalist Phyllis Entis reviewed an April 2023 FDA inspection of Nestlé Purina's Edmond, Oklahoma, plant, which the report says produces dry Cat Chow along with Friskies, Kit 'N Kaboodle, Kitten Chow, Purina ONE, and other dry lines. The inspector found no deviations or deficiencies and classified the visit 'No Action Indicated,' noting the plant tests finished product for Salmonella before release and requires corporate pre-approval of suppliers.

products.name: Friskies
products.description: Nestlé Purina's budget wet and dry cat food line, sold widely in US grocery and mass retail stores.

health.note: On December 26, 2025, third-party distributor Gold Star Distribution recalled all FDA-regulated products held at its Minneapolis warehouse, including several Friskies varieties such as Shreds, Pate, Prime Filet, and Surfin' & Turfin' canned cat food, after an FDA inspection found rodent droppings, rodent urine, and bird droppings in storage areas. The notice said no illnesses had been reported to date.

transparency.note: Independent food-safety journalist Phyllis Entis reviewed a June 2023 FDA inspection of Nestlé Purina's Crete, Nebraska, plant, which cans Friskies along with Alpo, Purina ONE, and Pro Plan Veterinary Diets. The inspector traced an earlier mislabeling recall to a conveyor motor malfunction that let a batch of cat food and dog food comingle before the retort step, meaning some cans received the wrong thermal process, and found the plant relied only on magnets to catch foreign material and had problems controlling residual chlorine in its cooling water.

products.name: Fancy Feast
products.description: Nestlé Purina's mainstream wet cat food line, sold in small cans through US grocery and mass retail stores.

health.note: On December 26, 2025, third-party distributor Gold Star Distribution recalled all FDA-regulated products held at its Minneapolis warehouse, including Fancy Feast Creamy Delight Salmon, Medleys Florentine, and Gravy Lovers canned cat food, after an FDA inspection found rodent droppings, rodent urine, and bird droppings in storage areas. The notice said no illnesses had been reported to date.

products.name: Meow Mix
products.description: J.M. Smucker's budget dry and wet cat food line, sold widely in US grocery and mass retail stores.

health.note: On December 26, 2025, third-party distributor Gold Star Distribution recalled all FDA-regulated products held at its Minneapolis warehouse, and the recall's product list includes several Meow Mix products, among them Meow Mix Original in 3.15 lb bags, after an FDA inspection found rodent droppings, rodent urine, and bird droppings in storage areas; the contamination was at the distributor's warehouse, not a Smucker plant, and the notice said no illnesses had been reported. Earlier: On April 9, 2021, The J.M. Smucker Co. recalled two lots of Meow Mix Original Choice Dry Cat Food 30 lb bags for potential Salmonella contamination. The products were sold at select Walmart stores in Illinois, Missouri, Nebraska, New Mexico, Oklahoma, Utah, Wisconsin, and Wyoming, and the company said it had received no reports of pet illness or adverse reaction.

products.name: 9Lives
products.description: A budget canned cat food line owned by Post Holdings since it bought 9Lives from J.M. Smucker in April 2023, one of the longest-running brands sold in US grocery and mass retail stores.

health.note: On December 26, 2025, third-party distributor Gold Star Distribution recalled all FDA-regulated products held at its Minneapolis warehouse, and the recall's product list includes 9 Lives cat food in 3.15 lb bags and 9 Lives canned chicken cat food, after an FDA inspection found rodent droppings, rodent urine, and bird droppings in storage areas; the contamination was at the distributor's warehouse, not a manufacturing plant, and the notice said no illnesses had been reported. Earlier: On December 7, 2018, The J.M. Smucker Co. recalled specific lots of 9Lives Protein Plus wet canned cat food, in Tuna & Chicken and Tuna & Liver varieties, for possible low levels of thiamine (vitamin B1). The products were distributed nationwide and the company said no illnesses related to the issue had been reported to date.

products.name: Special Kitty
products.description: Walmart's private label cat food, sold only at Walmart stores and Walmart.com; J.M. Smucker made it at the time of its 2019 recall and sold its private label pet food business to Post Holdings in April 2023.

accessibility.note: Walmart's own site groups Special Kitty under its 'Walmart Exclusive Pet Brands' category; the line is sold only at Walmart stores and Walmart.com, in dry, wet, and treat formats.

health.note: On December 5, 2019, The J.M. Smucker Co. recalled specific lots of Special Kitty Mixed Grill Dinner Pate and Special Kitty Surf & Turf Variety Pack wet canned cat food, distributed nationwide, for health concerns associated with ingredients the company said did not meet its quality and safety standards.

products.name: Iams
products.description: A Mars Petcare dry cat food sold widely in US grocery and mass retail stores.

health.note: On August 16, 2013, Procter & Gamble (Iams' owner at the time) recalled specific lots of Iams dry cat food, made during a 10-day window at a single manufacturing site, over Salmonella found in random testing. The lots represented about one-tenth of one percent of annual production and the company said no illnesses had been reported.

products.name: Taste of the Wild
products.description: A grain-free cat food line made by contract manufacturer Diamond Pet Foods, sold mainly through pet specialty and online retailers.

health.note: Diamond Pet Foods recalled all package sizes and formulas of Taste of the Wild made between December 9, 2011 and April 7, 2012 after Salmonella Infantis traced to its Gaston, South Carolina, plant. CDC's May 11, 2012 update on the multistate outbreak confirmed at least 15 human infections across nine states, with five people hospitalized, plus two further cases reported by Canadian health authorities.

transparency.note: eFoodAlert's account of the 2012 recall lists Taste of the Wild alongside Diamond's own house brands and other third-party labels such as Kirkland Signature, Canidae, and Solid Gold, all made at the same Gaston, South Carolina, plant, showing Diamond manufactures for many competing labels rather than Taste of the Wild alone.

products.name: Kirkland Signature
products.description: Costco's private label cat food, made by contract manufacturer Diamond Pet Foods and sold to Costco members.

accessibility.note: Costco's own 'About Kirkland Signature' page describes it as Costco's only private brand, sold exclusively through Costco's own warehouses and website; any Kirkland Signature product sold elsewhere was resold after first being bought at Costco, which requires a paid membership.

health.note: Diamond Pet Foods' 2012 recall for Salmonella Infantis contamination at its Gaston, South Carolina, plant named Kirkland Signature Super Premium Maintenance Cat Chicken & Rice Formula and Kirkland Signature Super Premium Healthy Weight Cat Formula, both with best-before dates of December 9, 2012 through January 31, 2013. CDC confirmed at least 15 human infections across nine states in the outbreak, with five people hospitalized.

products.name: Royal Canin
products.description: A Mars Petcare brand built around breed, age, and health-condition specific formulas, sold only through pet specialty stores and veterinary clinics.

accessibility.note: Royal Canin's own FAQ says its retail products cannot be bought directly from its facilities and are sold exclusively through pet specialty stores, while its Veterinary Exclusive formulas, including its feline renal and urinary diets, are only available by prescription through vet clinics; it is not sold in grocery stores.

products.name: Hill's Science Diet
products.description: Colgate-Palmolive's veterinary linked cat food brand, sold mainly through pet specialty stores, vet clinics, and online.

health.note: FDA's own notice about Hill's 2019 recall for excess vitamin D states that 'the recall is only for canned dog food and does not affect canned cat food, dry food (kibble), or treats.' A search of FDA's recalls, market withdrawals, and safety alerts listings on this date found no separate cat-food-specific recall for Hill's Science Diet or Prescription Diet; this is an absence of a public record, not independent proof the food carries no risk.

transparency.note: Hill's own site says it manufactures its recipes in Colgate-Palmolive owned and operated facilities and that its PhD nutritionists and veterinarians test recipes on site, with more than 900 dogs and cats involved in confirming final products before they ship; the page does not separate this claim by species.

products.name: Wellness
products.description: Wellness Pet Company's (formerly WellPet) natural-positioned canned cat food line, sold through pet specialty and online retailers.

health.note: On February 28, 2011, WellPet recalled all flavors and sizes of Wellness Canned Cat Food with best-by dates from April 14 through September 30, 2013, plus Wellness Canned Cat Food Chicken & Herring with two November 2013 best-by dates, after independent testing conducted with FDA in response to a consumer complaint found low levels of thiamine (vitamin B1). An estimated 21.6 million cans were affected.

products.name: Smalls
products.description: A fresh, human-grade cat food delivered by subscription, formulated with veterinary nutritionists and shipped refrigerated.

accessibility.note: Smalls' own site describes an online 'build your cat's fresh plan' subscription with home delivery and free shipping; the food is not sold in stores and needs to go in the fridge or freezer as soon as it arrives.

transparency.note: Smalls' own site says its recipes are 'formulated with veterinary nutritionists and certified complete and balanced for every life stage' and describes the food as gently cooked from real, whole ingredients with no preservatives or fillers; the page does not name the manufacturing facility.

products.name: Home-cooked, vet-formulated diet
products.description: Cooking a complete and balanced diet at home from ordinary grocery ingredients, using a recipe from a board certified veterinary nutritionist rather than buying a manufactured food.

accessibility.note: Home-cooked food uses ordinary grocery ingredients rather than depending on one manufacturer or retailer, so it can be made anywhere there is a kitchen and a grocery store. UC Davis researchers who evaluated 114 published cat food recipes found only 94 had enough detail for nutritional analysis, and cooking a diet daily takes far more time than opening a can or bag.

health.note: UC Davis researchers analyzed the 94 published homemade cat food recipes with enough detail to test and found that none met the National Research Council's recommended allowances for every essential nutrient for adult cats; many fell short on up to 19 nutrients, and several provided less than half the recommended amount of choline, iron, zinc, thiamin, vitamin E, or manganese. Seven percent of all 114 recipes called for a potentially toxic ingredient such as garlic, onion, or leek. Only five recipes, all written by veterinarians, came within one nutrient of meeting every requirement.

transparency.note: A home-cooked diet has no manufacturer between the ingredients and the bowl, so the cook buys and sees every ingredient directly. UC Davis's review found that turning this into a nutritionally complete diet in practice requires the kind of formulation that, in its sample, only recipes written by veterinarians came close to delivering.

products.name: Fromm
products.description: A family-owned Wisconsin maker of dry and canned cat food, sold only through independent pet stores and its own online shop.

accessibility.note: Fromm's own FAQ says 'Fromm products are sold exclusively through neighborhood pet specialty stores' or through its own GoFromm online shop; it is not sold in grocery, big box, or warehouse club stores.

health.note: A search of FDA's recall listings on this date (its current Animal & Veterinary recalls list, its current recalls, market withdrawals and safety alerts list, and its archived 2017 to 2021 recall notices) found no Fromm cat food recall. The same maker has recalled dog food three times since 2021, canned dog food for excess vitamin D in October 2021, a frozen dog food lot for possible plastic in December 2025, and two canned dog foods for metal in August 2026, none tied to reported illness, and its dog and cat food come from the same Wisconsin plants.

transparency.note: Fromm's own FAQ says it owns and operates two dry food and treat plants in Mequon and Columbus, Wisconsin, a frozen dog food plant in Columbus, and a wet food cannery in Eden, Wisconsin, and that every bag and can of its dog and cat food comes from one of those facilities rather than a contract manufacturer. A separate FAQ page names its PhD animal nutritionist, Dr. Danielle Opetz, as part of the team that formulates its diets.

links.label: Fromm FAQ: where it is made

products.name: Instinct
products.description: A raw-focused brand, formerly Nature's Variety, selling freeze-dried, kibble, and canned cat food made partly in its own Lincoln, Nebraska, plants.

health.note: A search of FDA's recall listings on this date (its current Animal & Veterinary recalls list, its current recalls, market withdrawals and safety alerts list, and its archived 2017 to 2021 recall notices) found no recall for Instinct or Nature's Variety cat food. The brand's last widely reported recall, in July 2015, was of one best-by date of Instinct Raw Chicken Formula frozen dog food after an FDA sample tested positive for Salmonella, with no illnesses reported.

transparency.note: Instinct's own FAQ describes 'company-owned manufacturing facilities in Lincoln, Nebraska' with SQF food safety and quality certifications, says its raw recipes go through high pressure processing and are tested by an external ISO 17025 certified lab before leaving the plant, and says its R&D staff consult its own board certified veterinary nutritionist. The FAQ does not say whether its kibble and canned lines are made in the same plants.

links.label: Food Safety News, July 2015 dog food recall

products.name: Open Farm
products.description: A brand built around humanely raised, traceable ingredients, with dry, wet, and freeze-dried cat food made by contract manufacturers.

health.note: A search of FDA's recall listings on this date (its current Animal & Veterinary recalls list, its current recalls, market withdrawals and safety alerts list, and its archived 2017 to 2021 recall notices) found no recall for Open Farm. This is an absence of a public record, not independent proof the food carries no risk.

transparency.note: Open Farm's own FAQ says it does not own its plants but uses vetted manufacturing partners in the United States, Canada, and Iceland, holds every batch until independent third-party lab tests clear it, and employs an in-house board certified veterinary nutritionist, Dr. Moran Tal-Gavriel, who formulates its recipes. It says 'Open Farm meets all the WSAVA guidelines for selecting a pet food, with the exception of feeding trials', which it says are now under way as at-home trials. Its transparency tool lets a buyer trace each ingredient and see pathogen test results by the lot code on the bag.

products.name: Natural Balance
products.description: A limited-ingredient focused brand, owned by J.M. Smucker until 2021 and now by Natural Balance Pet Foods, Inc., made partly in its own Brownwood, Texas, plant.

health.note: A search of FDA's recall listings on this date (its current Animal & Veterinary recalls list, its current recalls, market withdrawals and safety alerts list, and its archived 2017 to 2021 recall notices) found two Natural Balance cat food recalls. In July 2020 J.M. Smucker, then the owner, recalled one lot of Natural Balance Ultra Premium Chicken & Liver Paté canned cat food for excess choline chloride, and its notice said the company had received reports of adverse reactions. In May 2021 Natural Balance Pet Foods recalled L.I.D. Green Pea & Chicken dry cat food after a Minnesota state sample found possible Salmonella, with no illnesses reported. Nothing newer appears in FDA's current listing.

transparency.note: Natural Balance's own FAQ says most of its diets are made in the United States, either at its company-owned plant in Brownwood, Texas, or by selected manufacturing partners, without naming the partners or which products each makes; it says a PhD small animal nutritionist reviews every formula, that its Feed With Confidence program tests each batch and publishes the results, and that its feeding studies with a third-party facility are palatability and digestibility tests rather than full feeding trials.

products.name: Merrick
products.description: A Texas-founded natural positioned brand owned by Nestlé Purina, with dry and canned cat food.

health.note: A search of FDA's recall listings on this date (its current Animal & Veterinary recalls list, its current recalls, market withdrawals and safety alerts list, and its archived 2017 to 2021 recall notices) found no recall of Merrick cat food. The only Merrick entry is a May 2018 recall of specific production codes of beef dog treats for possible high levels of beef thyroid hormone.

transparency.note: Merrick's own FAQ says its recipes are formulated by an unnamed team of animal nutrition experts 'including PhDs, veterinarians, scientists and engineers' and its about page describes recipes crafted in Hereford, Texas, but neither page names the plants that make its dog and cat food. The site footer says Merrick trademarks are owned by Nestlé.

products.name: Weruva
products.description: A family-owned brand of wet cat food made in a human food facility, sold through specialty pet stores and online.

accessibility.note: Weruva's own where-to-buy page says its food 'can be found in the finest specialty pet retailers across the world' and asks shoppers to request it from their local store if it is not stocked; it does not list grocery or big box chains.

health.note: A search of FDA's recall listings on this date (its current Animal & Veterinary recalls list, its current recalls, market withdrawals and safety alerts list, and its archived 2017 to 2021 recall notices) found no recall for Weruva. This is an absence of a public record, not independent proof the food carries no risk.

transparency.note: Weruva's own family page says the company is wholly owned by David and Stacie Forman and that its food is produced in a human food facility using many of the ingredients and processes used for people food; its 'Why Weruva' page says the facilities meet strict international food standards. Neither page names the facility, its country, or a formulating nutritionist.

products.name: Tiki Cat
products.description: A wet-food-led cat food brand known for shredded meat and fish recipes, sold through pet stores and online.

health.note: A search of FDA's recall listings on this date (its current Animal & Veterinary recalls list, its current recalls, market withdrawals and safety alerts list, and its archived 2017 to 2021 recall notices) found no recall for Tiki Cat or Tiki Pets. This is an absence of a public record, not independent proof the food carries no risk.

transparency.note: Tiki Pets' own 'Why Feed Tiki' page describes its ingredients and their intended benefits in detail but names no manufacturing facility, manufacturer, or formulating nutritionist, and the site's where-to-buy page gives no further production detail.

products.name: Sheba
products.description: Mars Petcare's mainstream wet cat food line, sold in small trays and pouches through US grocery and mass retail stores.

health.note: A search of FDA's recall listings on this date (its current Animal & Veterinary recalls list, its current recalls, market withdrawals and safety alerts list, and its archived 2017 to 2021 recall notices) found no recall for Sheba. This is an absence of a public record, not independent proof the food carries no risk.

products.name: Blue Buffalo
products.description: A General Mills owned brand of dry and wet cat food marketed on natural ingredient claims, sold through pet specialty and mass retail stores.

health.note: A search of FDA's recall listings on this date (its current Animal & Veterinary recalls list, its current recalls, market withdrawals and safety alerts list, and its archived 2017 to 2021 recall notices) found no Blue Buffalo cat food recall; the only Blue Buffalo entry is a March 2017 recall of one lot of BLUE Wilderness Rocky Mountain Recipe Red Meat Dinner wet dog food for high levels of beef thyroid hormone.

transparency.note: Blue Buffalo's own FAQ says it makes food in two of its own plants, in Joplin, Missouri, and Richmond, Indiana, uses other US manufacturing partners, and has a select number of products made by partners in Thailand, and that recipes are developed by on-staff veterinarians and PhD-level animal nutritionists; it does not say which products come from which plant. Separately, Blue Buffalo settled a class action over by-product claims for $32 million in 2015 without admitting wrongdoing, as noted on its dog food entry.

products.name: Purina Pro Plan
products.description: Nestlé Purina's vet recommended cat food line, sold at pet specialty stores, some vet clinics, and online.

health.note: A search of FDA's recall listings on this date (its current Animal & Veterinary recalls list, its current recalls, market withdrawals and safety alerts list, and its archived 2017 to 2021 recall notices) found no Pro Plan cat food recall. The most recent Pro Plan recall FDA posted was for dog food: Purina Pro Plan Veterinary Diets EL Elemental dry dog food, recalled in February 2023 and expanded in March 2023 for excess vitamin D from a supplier's premix. Purina's Cat Chow, Friskies, and Fancy Feast were in the December 2025 Gold Star distributor recall, but Pro Plan was not on that list.

transparency.note: Independent food-safety journalist Phyllis Entis reviewed 2023 FDA inspection records for the Nestlé Purina plants that make Pro Plan and Purina ONE: the Edmond, Oklahoma, dry food plant, which makes both lines for cats, was classified 'No Action Indicated' with no deficiencies; the Clinton, Iowa, kibble plant had not tested an ADM vitamin premix before use; and the Crete, Nebraska, plant that cans Purina ONE and Pro Plan dog and cat food had a conveyor fault that let a cat food and a dog food mix before the retort step.

products.name: Purina ONE
products.description: A mid tier Nestlé Purina cat food line positioned above Cat Chow, sold at the same grocery and mass retail stores.

health.note: A search of FDA's recall listings on this date (its current Animal & Veterinary recalls list, its current recalls, market withdrawals and safety alerts list, and its archived 2017 to 2021 recall notices) found no Purina ONE cat food recall, and Purina ONE was not among the Purina products on the December 2025 Gold Star distributor recall list.

transparency.note: Independent food-safety journalist Phyllis Entis reviewed 2023 FDA inspection records for the Nestlé Purina plants that make Pro Plan and Purina ONE: the Edmond, Oklahoma, dry food plant, which makes both lines for cats, was classified 'No Action Indicated' with no deficiencies; the Clinton, Iowa, kibble plant had not tested an ADM vitamin premix before use; and the Crete, Nebraska, plant that cans Purina ONE and Pro Plan dog and cat food had a conveyor fault that let a cat food and a dog food mix before the retort step.

products.name: Rachael Ray Nutrish
products.description: A grocery-store cat food line owned by Post Holdings since it bought Nutrish from J.M. Smucker in April 2023.

health.note: A search of FDA's recall listings on this date (its current Animal & Veterinary recalls list, its current recalls, market withdrawals and safety alerts list, and its archived 2017 to 2021 recall notices) found no recall for Nutrish in the current listing. Earlier history: in June 2015 Ainsworth Pet Nutrition, then the maker, recalled five Nutrish wet cat food varieties for excess vitamin D from fish ingredients after 11 reports of illness, according to its own recall notice, and suspended production of those varieties pending reformulation.

transparency.note: Nutrish's own FAQ answers 'Who owns and manufactures' the food only by saying Post Brands Pet Care, LLC bought it from J.M. Smucker in April 2023; it names no plant, though it says independent third parties audit the food safety programs at each manufacturing facility. Smucker's April 2023 closing release says the sale included its Meadville, Pennsylvania, and Lawrence, Kansas, pet food plants.
